title: Quant shadow cohort strategy and rollback playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines Redwood's standard approach for running shadow (non-production) deployments of quantized model artifacts against cohorted traffic, how we measure fidelity and key regressions, and the fast rollback / deep-diagnosis procedures when signal thresholds are exceeded. It is intended for ML Engineers, Oncall Evaluators, and Platform operators involved in quant migrations, mixed-precision rollouts, or model compression initiatives.

Goals:
- Validate quantized model variants against realistic traffic without impacting production routing.
- Detect meaningful quality regressions early using per-slice fidelity and stability signals.
- Provide a deterministic, low-friction rollback path and diagnostics bundle to accelerate root cause.
- Ensure ownership, alerts, and cost controls are clearly defined for every shadow cohort.

Scope:
- Applies to any quantization profile promoted from quant-tuner to the staging artifact registry.
- Covers Dedicated, Private, and Hosted shadow modes (shadow-inplace and sidecar-shadow).
- Excludes A/B tests where traffic split exposes customers to quant artifacts directly.

Roles & Ownership:
| Role | Responsibilities | Primary Service | Contact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quant Owner | Prepare quant profile, baseline audits, preflight checks | quant-tuner | @quant-team |
| Shadow Orchestrator Owner | Configure cohort, start shadow job, apply routing policy | shadow-sequencer | @infra-platform |
| Evaluator (Oncall) | Monitor fidelity signals, triage alerts, run diagnostics | eval-orchestrator | @applied-ml |
| Rollback Lead | Authorize and execute rollback, coordinate postmortem | release-engineering | @sre |

Key Signals & Thresholds (telemetry names used by alerting):
| Signal | Computation | Alert threshold (per-slice) | Severity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FidelityDelta | 1 - (mean_similarity_quant / mean_similarity_fp) * 100% | > 2.0% | P1 |
| ResponseStabilityIndex (RSI) | 1 - average token-level divergence | > 0.08 | P1 |
| EmbeddingCohortDrift | cosine shift between embeddings (median) | > 0.03 | P2 |
| LatencyTailIncrease | 95th percentile quant / 95th percentile baseline | > 1.15x | P2 |
| ErrorRateDelta | (quant_errors - baseline_errors) / baseline | > 2.0% absolute | P1 |

Cohort Selection & Shadow Modes:
- Deterministic user cohorts: select by tenant_id hash ranges (recommended for tenant-isolated features).
- Behavioral cohorts: slices defined by workload fingerprint (e.g., long-context, multimodal, function-calling).
- Traffic mirroring modes:
  1. sidecar-shadow: mirror requests to a sidecar instance running quant artifact; responses discarded but telemetry ingested. Low isolation, minimal infra changes.
  2. in-cluster-shadow: route duplicates to an isolated pool of GPUs with identical infra; useful for performance comparisons.
  3. sample-replay: replay recorded requests through quant artifact for deterministic comparisons (used for heavy slices).

Shadow Execution Procedure (step-by-step):
1. Preflight (Quant Owner)
   - Run quant-lint and quant-sanity checks locally; ensure diff coverage >= 95% for smoke probes.
   - Register artifact in artifact-registry with tag: quant/<model>-<profile>-<YYYYMMDD>.
   - Produce baseline snapshot: store baseline embeddings, tokenization checks, and cost profile. Use CLI: 
     - samctl quant-lint --artifact <artifact> --probe-set smoke-v1 --output /tmp/quant-audit.json
2. Configure cohort (Shadow Orchestrator Owner)
   - Create cohort config: name, selector (tenant_hash_range or probe_slice), retention TTL, telemetry sinks. Example YAML: 

```yaml
cohort_name: quant-shadow-longcontext-2026-01
selector: probe_slice:long_context_v2
mode: sidecar-shadow
max_rps: 20
telemetry_sinks: [eval-telemetry, observability-ingest]
owners: [quant-team, eval-oncall]
```

3. Launch shadow job (Shadow Orchestrator Owner)
   - Use shadow-sequencer UI or CLI: 
     - shadowctl start --cohort cohort_name --artifact quant/<tag> --dry-run=false
   - Confirm mirrored traffic appears in eval-orchestrator with correct cohort tags.
4. Monitoring window (Evaluator)
   - Minimum observation window: 48 hours or until 1000 weighted probes per slice (whichever first).
   - Primary dashboards: Quant Shadow Overview, Per-Slice Fidelity, Token Divergence Heatmap.
   - Expected stability band: FidelityDelta <= 1.0% for majority slices; any P1 hit triggers immediate triage.

Promotion Checklist (to canary / limited production):
- Automated checks passed: quant-sanity, tokenization parity, memory footprint <= baseline * 0.95 (if expected).
- No P1 alerts for 72 hours and all P2 alerts investigated and closed.
- Cost delta analyzed: per-token GPU cost change documented and approved by finance for Reserved deployments.
- Rollout plan with traffic ramp steps and automatic fallback policy created in Redwood Console.

Alert Triage & Diagnosis (Evaluator):
1. When a P1 triggers (FidelityDelta or ErrorRateDelta):
   - Capture a diagnostics bundle using eval-orchestrator: 
     - evalctl bundle --cohort <name> --time-range last_60m --output /tmp/diag-<id>.tar.gz
   - Run differential replay against the full-fp artifact and quant artifact to produce per-example diff.
   - Use the probe-compare tool to classify failure modes: tokenization mismatch, hallucination-increase, truncation-induced errors, or numerical-instability.
2. If diagnostics indicate quant profile bug (e.g., rounding instabilities, kernel mismatch):
   - Notify Quant Owner and create a P0 ticket with the diagnostics bundle and replication steps.
3. If triage cannot identify cause within 2 hours or regression affects >5% of a critical slice: escalate to Rollback Lead.

Rollback Runbook (fast path):
- Eligibility: P1 fidelity/error alert affecting a critical slice or sustained > 3% overall fidelity regression for 2 hours.
- Steps: 
  1. Announce intent on #incident-ml and @page owners; mark the shadow job as suspended in shadow-sequencer.
  2. If in-cluster-shadow: drain quant pool using k8s label toggle: 
     - kubectl label nodes quant-pool action=drain --overwrite
     - shadowctl suspend --cohort <name> --reason "auto-rollback-fidelity"
  3. For canary production promotions: flip the routing policy to the prior artifact tag using release-engineering CLI: 
     - releasectl revert --service <service-name> --to-tag <previous-tag> --synchronous
  4. Collect post-rollback telemetry and confirm FidelityDelta returns to baseline within 30 minutes.
  5. Schedule a postmortem within 48 hours with Quant Owner, Evaluator, and Rollback Lead.

Diagnostics bundle contents (minimum):
- request/response pairs for failing probes (JSONL)
- tokenization traces for both artifacts (token ids, offsets)
- model logits and per-token probabilities for sample subset
- embedding vectors for embedding-drift slices
- environment snapshot: kernel versions, CUDA, cuDNN, quant backend config

Common Failure Modes & Mitigations:
- Tokenization drift: ensure tokenizer packaging is pinned and included in artifact. If present, update packaging and re-run shadow.
- KV-cache mismatch: run sequence length stress tests; if state misalignment found, fall back to in-cluster-shadow to isolate serving runtime differences.
- Numerical instability in extreme long-context: tighten quant clipping thresholds; consult kernel-team for custom kernel fallback.
- Perf regressions from fused kernels: run micro-benchmarks in perf-suite and adjust kernel selection policy in compilation config.

Postmortem & Continuous Improvement:
- Postmortem template fields: summary, impact (slices affected), root cause, detection latency, mitigation, follow-up actions, owner for fixes.
- Metrics to record for each migration: pre/post fidelity, deployment cost delta, rollback frequency, mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to remediate (MTTR).
- Quarterly review: Quant migration health report to be included in platform roadmap review (owners: quant-team, infra).

Appendices:
A. Example quant profile (snippet):
```json
{
  "profile_name": "q8_256_clip_v2",
  "method": "int8_dynamic",
  "clip_threshold": 6.0,
  "per_channel": true,
  "weight_granularity": "per-tensor",
  "kernel_hint": "fused_attention_v3"
}
```

B. Command cheatsheet:
- shadowctl start --cohort <name> --artifact <tag>
- shadowctl suspend --cohort <name> --reason <text>
- evalctl bundle --cohort <name> --time-range <range> --output <file>
- quantctl lint --artifact <tag> --probe-set smoke-v1

C. Related diagnostics scripts: probe-compare, quant-diff-inspector, embedding-shift-analyzer (available in tools/internal/quant-utils).

Document history:
- 2026-01-12: created by Aisha Patel (quant migration alpha run notes).
- 2026-02-20: updated thresholds and rollback cadence after shadow run Q2-2026.

Contacts and escalation links:
- #quant-team (Slack), #eval-oncall (Slack), runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/quant-shadow-runbook

If you are about to use this playbook for the first time, run a tabletop drill with release-engineering and eval-oncall using the included sample cohort YAML.
